sections.content: How many people stayed in Eckington after gaining qualifications?

Eckington is a small town in the East Midlands. Eckington does not have its own university.

Eckington has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Eckington ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 395 state-school pupils from Eckington who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 85 (22%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 155 (39%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Eckington to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Eckington's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Eckington in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Eckington's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left the East Midlands
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 46% of graduates and 37% of qualified non-graduates living in Eckington had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 65 graduates and 150 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Eckington. This is compared with the 85 graduates and 155 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 54% of the graduates had also lived in Eckington as GCSE pupils, while 46% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Eckington in 2018 to 2019, 67% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 37% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
